name: Isolated Hereditary Giant Platelet Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Hereditary Giant Platelet Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of abnormally large platelets (giant platelets) on peripheral blood smear
Mild to moderate thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically between 50-150 x10^9/L
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Normal platelet aggregation studies excluding acquired platelet dysfunction
Exclusion of other causes of thrombocytopenia and giant platelets such as immune thrombocytopenia or MYH9-related disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of giant platelets and thrombocytopenia with supportive family history and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but is not always available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Giant platelets on peripheral blood smear
searchTerms: very large platelets in blood test
giant blood cells seen under microscope
abnormally big platelets in blood smear

common.symptomName: Mucocutaneous bleeding tendency (e.g., easy bruising, epistaxis)
searchTerms: tendency to bleed from mucous membranes
bleeding lasts long after small cuts

occasional.symptomName: Mild anemia secondary to chronic bleeding
searchTerms: mild low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia caused by chronic blood loss
slight anemia due to ongoing bleeding
low energy due to blood loss
rare episodes of blood vessel blockage
unusual clotting in veins or arteries

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing giant platelets
imaging: Usually normal; splenomegaly rare but may be detected on abdominal ultrasound
genetic: Mutations in genes related to platelet cytoskeleton and membrane (e.g., MYH9 excluded in isolated form)
Genetic testing may identify causative mutations in some cases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of additional features such as hearing loss, nephropathy, and cataracts
Defective platelet adhesion due to GPIb deficiency

redFlags: Severe bleeding disproportionate to platelet count
Sudden onset of thrombocytopenia without family history
Signs of systemic illness or organ involvement
references: Balduini CL, Savoia A. Hereditary macrothrombocytopenias: an update. Haematologica. 2012;97(7):963-967.
